chunks: Therefore, He alone knows what is in the wombs, whether male or female, ugly or handsome, generous or miserly, wretched or happy, and who will be the fuel for Hell and who will be in the company of the Prophets in Paradise. This is the knowledge of the hidden things which is not known to anyone save Allah. All else is that whose knowledge Allah passed on to His Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and he passed it on to me, and prayed for me that my bosom may retain it and my ribs may hold it.
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Allah's knowledge of the unseen and the knowledge given to the Prophets and Imams?
ai.summary: This passage delineates the hierarchy of knowledge by contrasting Allah's exclusive, absolute knowledge of the unseen (ghayb al-mutlaq)—specifically the foetus's gender, character, and eternal destination—with the contingent knowledge (ghayb al-mu'tabar) transmitted to the Prophet and inherited by the Imam. It highlights the Shia doctrine of the Imam's spiritual capacity to preserve and internalize this divine wisdom, serving as a bridge between the Creator's absolute omniscience and human prophetic revelation.
